questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using a single fixed pulley to lift a bucket of water from a deep well?

options.text: To multiply the applied effort force
To change the direction of the applied force
To multiply the speed of motion
To reduce the total work done on the load

questions.explanation: A single fixed pulley has a mechanical advantage and velocity ratio of 1. It does not multiply force or speed; its main function is to change the direction of the effort force (pulling downward instead of lifting upward).

questions.question: Which of the following simple machines belongs to the inclined plane family?
questions.explanation: Simple machines are categorized into two primary families: inclined planes (ramp, wedge, screw) and levers (lever, wheel and axle, pulley). A wedge consists of two inclined planes placed back-to-back.

questions.question: How is the Mechanical Advantage (M.A) of a simple machine defined?

options.text: The ratio of effort distance to load distance
The ratio of load force to effort force
The ratio of work output to work input
The product of effort force and load force

questions.explanation: Mechanical Advantage (M.A) is defined as the ratio of the output force (load) exerted by the machine to the input force (effort) applied to the machine (M.A = Load / Effort).

questions.question: Which class of lever has the load situated between the fulcrum and the effort point?
questions.explanation: In a second-class lever (such as a wheelbarrow or nutcracker), the load is located between the fulcrum at one end and the effort applied at the other end.

questions.question: Why is the efficiency of any real-world simple machine always less than 100%?

options.text: Because the load force is always smaller than the effort force.
Because work input is destroyed by the machine.
Because some input energy is converted into non-useful thermal energy due to friction.
Because the velocity ratio is always smaller than the mechanical advantage.

questions.explanation: In real machines, friction between moving parts transforms part of the input work into non-useful thermal energy, making work output less than work input and efficiency less than 100%.

questions.question: A lever is used to lift a 600 N load by applying an effort force of 150 N. What is the Mechanical Advantage (M.A) of the lever?
questions.explanation: Mechanical Advantage (M.A) = Load / Effort = 600 N / 150 N = 4.0.

questions.question: An inclined plane has a length of 12 m along its slope and raises an object to a vertical height of 3 m. Assuming no friction, what is the Velocity Ratio (V.R) of this inclined plane?
questions.explanation: For an inclined plane, Velocity Ratio (V.R) = length of slope / height raised = 12 m / 3 m = 4.0.

questions.question: A wheel and axle system has a wheel radius of 40 cm and an axle radius of 8 cm. What is the Velocity Ratio (V.R) of this machine?
questions.explanation: For a wheel and axle system, Velocity Ratio (V.R) = radius of wheel / radius of axle = 40 cm / 8 cm = 5.0.

questions.question: A machine has a Mechanical Advantage (M.A) of 3.0 and a Velocity Ratio (V.R) of 4.0. What is the efficiency of this machine expressed as a percentage?
A 15 cm long wedge with a thickness of 3 cm is driven into a wooden block. What is the Velocity Ratio (V.R) of the wedge?
questions.explanation: For a wedge, Velocity Ratio (V.R) = penetration length / thickness = 15 cm / 3 cm = 5.0.

questions.question: A compound pulley system (block and tackle) uses 4 supporting rope segments to hold a movable load. If an effort of 200 N is needed to raise a 640 N load, what is the efficiency of the pulley system?
questions.explanation: V.R = number of supporting rope segments = 4. M.A = Load / Effort = 640 N / 200 N = 3.2. Efficiency η = (M.A / V.R) × 100% = (3.2 / 4) × 100% = 80.0%.

questions.question: A second-class lever has a total length of 1.5 m from the fulcrum to the effort handle. A load of 900 N is placed on the lever at a distance of 0.3 m from the fulcrum. Assuming 100% efficiency, what effort force is required to lift the load?
questions.explanation: Effort arm d_E = 1.5 m, Load arm d_L = 0.3 m. V.R = d_E / d_L = 1.5 / 0.3 = 5. At 100% efficiency, M.A = V.R = 5. Therefore, Effort = Load / M.A = 900 N / 5 = 180 N.

questions.question: An inclined plane of length 10 m and height 2 m is used to move a 500 N barrel. Due to friction, the efficiency of the slope is 80%. What input effort force is required to push the barrel up the ramp?
questions.explanation: V.R = slope length / height = 10 m / 2 m = 5. Efficiency η = 0.80. M.A = η × V.R = 0.80 × 5 = 4.0. Effort = Load / M.A = 500 N / 4.0 = 125 N.

questions.question: A screw jack has a pitch of 2.0 mm and is operated using a lever handle of length 28 cm. Taking π ≈ 22/7, what is the Ideal Mechanical Advantage (IMA) of the screw jack?
questions.explanation: IMA of a screw = (2 × π × r) / pitch. Radius r = 28 cm = 280 mm, pitch p = 2.0 mm. IMA = [2 × (22/7) × 280] / 2.0 = (2 × 22 × 40) / 2 = 880.

questions.question: A wheel and axle system with a wheel radius of 50 cm and axle radius of 10 cm is used to draw water from a well. An effort force of 120 N is applied to the wheel to raise a 480 N bucket of water. How much work is lost as thermal energy due to friction when the bucket is raised through a height of 5 m?
questions.explanation: V.R = R / r = 50 / 10 = 5. To lift load by d_L = 5 m, effort moves d_E = V.R × d_L = 5 × 5 m = 25 m. Work input = Effort × d_E = 120 N × 25 m = 3000 J. Work output = Load × d_L = 480 N × 5 m = 2400 J. Lost work (thermal energy due to friction) = Work input - Work output = 3000 J - 2400 J = 600 J.
